excerpt: Hitting a deer and swerving to avoid one are covered by different policies. How animal collisions work in Georgia and South Carolina.
keyTakeaways: Hitting an animal directly is covered by comprehensive insurance, while swerving into another object falls under collision coverage. Livestock owners can be liable under O.C.G.A. § 4-3-3 (Georgia) and S.C. Code § 47-7-120 (South Carolina). Georgia allows 2 years for injury claims (O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33) and South Carolina allows 3 years (S.C. Code § 15-3-530). Minimum liability-only insurance does not cover animal strike damage to your vehicle.

faqs.question: Does comprehensive insurance cover hitting a deer?
faqs.answer: Yes. Directly striking an animal is typically covered under comprehensive insurance, not collision. You will pay your comprehensive deductible, and this type of claim generally does not increase your insurance premiums.

faqs.question: What happens if I swerve to avoid an animal and hit another car?
faqs.answer: If you swerve to avoid an animal and hit another vehicle or object, the damage falls under collision coverage, not comprehensive. You may be found partially at fault for the swerve, which could increase your insurance rates.

faqs.question: Can I sue a livestock owner if their animal caused my accident?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Georgia law (O.C.G.A. § 4-3-3) and South Carolina law (S.C. Code § 47-7-120), livestock owners have a duty to keep their animals properly fenced. If they fail to do so and their animal causes a car accident, they can be held liable for injuries and damages.

faqs.question: Does liability-only insurance cover animal accident damage to my car?
faqs.answer: No. If you carry only the minimum liability insurance required by Georgia or South Carolina law, you have no coverage for damage to your own vehicle from an animal strike. Only comprehensive coverage protects against animal collision damage.

faqs.question: What should I do after hitting a deer in Georgia or South Carolina?
faqs.answer: Pull over safely, call 911, do not approach the animal, photograph the damage and scene, check for injuries, and file a comprehensive insurance claim promptly. A police report strengthens your claim.

faqs.question: When is deer strike season in Georgia and South Carolina?
faqs.answer: Deer-vehicle collisions peak during October through December — the deer mating season (rut). During this period, deer are more active and more likely to cross roadways, especially at dawn and dusk.
